entry.title: herdr × Git Worktree: A Practical Multi-Agent Concurrent Development Environment
entry.content:
💡 阅读中文原版 (Chinese Version)

When running multiple coding agents concurrently, the hard part is not spinning them up—it is surviving three structural bottlenecks: file collisions, state blindness, and fragile sessions. Starting from two foundational primitives—git worktree and herdr—this article presents the production project-level concurrent development environment I run daily: multiple isolated worktrees backed by a single repository, on-demand agent assignment per task, and centralized merge convergence in the main repository. While verified on herdr 0.9.5 / macOS, the architecture and commands apply across platforms.

1. The Three Walls of Multi-Agent Concurrency

Spin up five terminal windows to run coding agents in parallel and you quickly descend into a game of whack-a-mole: the agent in Window A is refactoring a shared module while the agent in Window B silently overwrites the exact same file; the agent in Window C has been stalled on a dangerous-command permission prompt for thirty minutes, which you only discover when you manually alt-tab into it; worst of all, accidentally closing a terminal window kills a half-finished refactoring session along with its entire live execution state.

Deconstructing these failure modes reveals three underlying infrastructure walls:

BottleneckTypical SymptomRoot Cause
File CollisionsTwo agents edit the same repo simultaneously; Agent A’s half-written changes are overwritten by Agent B or break the buildMultiple concurrent processes share a single physical working directory (Working Tree)
State BlindnessYou can only tell which agent is thinking, blocked on a prompt, or finished by manually cycling through windowsTraditional terminal multiplexers only forward raw PTY byte streams and have no concept of an “agent”
Fragile SessionsClosing a terminal window or dropping an SSH connection sends SIGHUP, killing the agent process and wiping the workspaceAgent processes are attached directly to the foreground window’s PTY session without a persistent daemon layer

You do not need to reinvent the wheel to solve this. Two off-the-shelf tools address the problem at orthogonal layers: git worktree handles physical filesystem isolation, while herdr handles agent state awareness and background session persistence. Combined under a strict set of engineering disciplines, they form a complete multi-agent concurrent development environment.

2. Foundation I: Git Worktree — One Repository, Multiple Working Trees

2.1 What It Solves

When two agents need to modify the same repository concurrently, the three common workarounds all carry steep penalties:

  • Cloning multiple independent copies: Doubles disk usage, hides local commits from other copies, and forces every synchronization through the remote origin;
  • Switching branches in the same directory (git checkout): Inherently serial—true concurrency is impossible;
  • The git stash dance: git stash → switch branch → edit → git stash pop, where merge conflict probability scales exponentially with concurrency.

git worktree is Git’s native architectural answer: a single .git object database mounted across multiple independent working directories (checkouts). Each worktree has its own physical directory and checked-out branch, while sharing the underlying .git/objects store and refs—any commit made in one worktree is instantaneously visible to every other worktree for merging or rebasing at zero network synchronization cost.

2.2 Essential Commands at a Glance

2.3 Two Iron Rules

  1. Commit locally inside worktrees; never push from them: Each worktree is responsible solely for advancing local commits on its dedicated task branch. Merging and remote pushing are performed exclusively from the main repository. Allowing multiple worktrees to push independently quickly corrupts remote branch history and triggers colliding CI runs.
  2. Converge all merges in the main repository: Keep the main repository anchored on master/main and run git merge --no-edit <branch> sequentially. Resolve any conflicts centrally in the main repo while preserving valid changes from both sides—never use --ours or --theirs inside a worktree to blindly wipe out parallel work.

2.4 Trap #1: gitignored Files Do Not Carry Over Automatically

Files ignored by .gitignore—such as .env environment variables, local private keys, and untracked local agent configurations (e.g., .claude/settings.local.json)—do not exist in newly created worktrees. Left unaddressed, builds and agents inside a fresh worktree will immediately fail due to missing environment variables or dropped MCP servers. Section 4.3 provides a one-command broadcast script from the main repository to eliminate this friction.

3. Foundation II: herdr — An Agent-Aware Terminal Multiplexer

3.1 Core Positioning

herdr is a single-binary terminal multiplexer written in Rust purpose-built for AI coding agents. Unlike traditional terminal tools that merely forward raw PTY byte streams, it gets one critical abstraction right—it natively understands whether a pane is running a coding agent and tracks that agent’s exact lifecycle state.

Under the hood, it uses a client/server architecture: a background herdr server daemon owns the PTY file descriptors for all panes, while the foreground TUI is merely an attached rendering view. This separation is the source of its persistence—you can close the terminal window at any time while your agent processes continue running undisturbed inside the background server.

3.2 Core Domain Model

ConceptEngineering Definition
serverThe background daemon owning all local PTY sessions; a single server hosts any number of repositories simultaneously
workspaceA project-level container, typically mapped 1:1 to a Git repository; independent of the directory from which you invoke herdr
paneA terminal split pane capable of running either a standard interactive shell or a managed coding agent
agentAn agent process recognized and tracked by herdr, specified via --kind (claude / codex / pi / opencode / antigravity-cli, etc.—24 built-in kinds as of v0.9.5)
stateThe agent’s real-time lifecycle state: working / blocked / idle / done

3.3 Three Tiers of Value

  1. Session Persistence (Foundational Value): Close your MacBook lid, survive an SSH drop, or accidentally close the terminal app—your background agent tasks keep running. Run herdr to re-attach in one second with your exact split layout intact.
  2. Global Status Board (Core Differentiator): The left sidebar renders real-time status indicators for every project and agent pane (specifically amber blocked and green done lights), eliminating the cognitive overhead of polling windows.
  3. Agent Self-Orchestration (Emergent Value): Once equipped with the official herdr Skill, a primary agent running inside a pane can invoke the herdr CLI to split new panes, spawn helper agents, dispatch subtasks, block until completion, and harvest results—a closed loop that is notoriously brittle to script with traditional terminal multiplexers.

Common Misconception: Do not treat herdr merely as a “multi-worktree launcher with completion alerts.” Worktree isolation is an opt-in helper feature, whereas the three tiers above are the core engine. Furthermore, if you skip herdr integration install, state detection falls back to brittle screen-scraping heuristics, degrading accuracy significantly.

3.4 Installation & Authoritative State Integration

On macOS, install the binary via Homebrew and immediately register the official lifecycle integrations for your primary agent CLIs:

Running herdr integration install injects lightweight lifecycle callbacks into each agent’s global configuration (for example, the hooks block in ~/.claude/settings.json). Whenever the agent starts executing, pauses on a permission prompt, or finishes a turn, it notifies herdr server over local IPC in milliseconds—making blocked and done transitions 100% deterministic.

3.5 Interaction Model & Essential Keybindings

herdr treats the mouse as a first-class citizen: click to focus panes, drag borders to resize splits, right-click to open the pane management menu, and click-drag to copy text without memorizing a single keybinding.

For keyboard navigation, it uses a classic Prefix modal pattern (default prefix is Ctrl+B—press and release Ctrl+B first, then press the action key, rather than holding Ctrl+B down):

KeybindingAction
prefix + vSplit vertically to the right (create right pane)
prefix + -Split horizontally downward (create bottom pane)
prefix + cCreate a new Tab inside the current Workspace
prefix + Shift+GInteractively create a new Git Worktree
prefix + ?Toggle the real-time keybinding cheat sheet overlay
prefix + qDetach from the current client view (background tasks continue; closing the window does the same)

Persistence in Practice: Press prefix + q or Cmd+W to close the terminal window at any time → run herdr from any directory to re-attach right where you left off. Only an explicit herdr server stop terminates the background daemon and all running panes.

3.6 Status Light Semantics & Attention Shift

Status LightLifecycle MeaningYour Action Policy
workingThinking, reasoning, or executing tool callsIgnore—let it run
blockedStalled on a dangerous-command approval or interactive question, waiting for your keystrokeSwitch immediately and unblock (highest priority)
idleTurn completed and you have already inspected the pane; standing byReady for the next prompt
doneTask just finished and you have not yet viewed the output (automatically transitions to idle once focused)Switch over when convenient to review results

This state machine transforms daily developer flow: you can keep agents running across three or four repositories while focusing deeply on architecture or documentation, keeping the sidebar in your peripheral vision—ignoring everything except blocked and done.

3.7 Host Terminal Selection & Configuration: Why Tabby Wins

Because herdr is a TUI application running inside a terminal emulator, the host terminal’s event-forwarding behavior directly dictates day-to-day ergonomics.

My daily workflow has two non-negotiable requirements:

  1. Full right-click mouse management for panes: splitting, closing, and zooming panes entirely via the right-click context menu;
  2. Direct Cmd+V clipboard image pasting: pasting error screenshots and architecture sketches straight into multimodal agents like Claude Code.

Testing the major macOS terminal emulators against these two hard criteria yielded a clear winner:

Host TerminalCmd+V Image Paste into Agent inside herdrRight-Click & Protocol SupportVerdict
Tabby (Electron)Works end-to-end (clipboard paste is handled at the app layer without being swallowed by the PTY)100% passthrough to herdr once Tabby’s native right-click menu is disabledPrimary Choice (Zero Compromise)
GhosttyBroken (Cmd+V only delivers a literal "v" character; image pasting fails both inside herdr and in bare CLI)Native Kitty keyboard protocol and mouse passthroughDisqualified for screenshot-heavy workflows
WarpConstrained by custom input boxBlock input model hijacks mouse and key events, conflicting with TUI multiplexersIncompatible
macOS Terminal.appNo rich clipboard image passthroughLacks Kitty Keyboard Protocol; incomplete modifier key forwardingNot Recommended

Three-Step Zero-Friction Tabby Setup:

  1. Open Tabby Settings → Application, locate “Show menu on right click”, and turn it off (sets rightClick: 'off' in config). Once disabled, right-clicking inside any pane opens herdr’s native split/pane menu;
  2. Recommended typography & theme: Maple Mono NF CN paired with the Catppuccin Mocha color scheme;
  3. Note for Pure Keyboard Users: If you do not rely on Cmd+V image pasting and prefer keyboard-driven workflows, your host terminal must satisfy three requirements: native mouse event passthrough, Kitty Keyboard Protocol support (use Kitty ≥ 0.33 or Alacritty ≥ 0.15.0, as older Alacritty releases suffer from duplicate key-release byte bugs), and mapping macOS Option as Meta.

4. Putting It Together: Project-Level Concurrent Environment Design

4.1 Directory & Session Topology

Combining git worktree with herdr produces a clean, standardized on-disk and in-memory topology for every project:

A single global herdr server hosts all of your active repositories (one Workspace per repo) alongside the concurrent worktree panes underneath each project—giving you a single-pane-of-glass command center across every running agent.

4.2 Five Engineering Design Principles

  1. Bind Workspaces to projects, never to agents: One Git repository maps to one Workspace. Running multiple projects in parallel simply means multiple Workspaces coexisting side by side.
  2. Create Worktrees strictly for concurrency isolation: When a single agent works on a project, run it directly in the main repository without any worktrees. Spin up worktrees only when two or more agents need to modify the same repository simultaneously.

    Hard-earned lesson: Early on, I named directories after agent types (myproject-claude, myproject-opencode). The moment I wanted to run Claude in the second directory, the directory name contradicted the process inside it. A directory should represent “Isolated Copy #N of the repository (wt-1, wt-2)”, completely decoupled from which agent works inside it.

  3. Assign agents on the fly; keep slot numbers agnostic: wt-1 is just a slot index. Whether that pane runs claude for feature work today, codex for bug fixes tomorrow, or opencode for unit tests next week is decided at launch via the command or --kind flag—the directory stays put.
  4. Use the main repository exclusively for convergence: Inside worktrees, agents may only run git commit—never git push. Branch merging, conflict resolution, and remote pushing happen centrally in the main repository (enforcing Section 2.3 at the environment level).
  5. Broadcast untracked configs one-way from the main repo: Treat the main repository as the Single Source of Truth (SSOT) for gitignored files (.env, local keys, MCP configs) and broadcast them into worktree slots via a sync script, solving Section 2.4 cleanly.

4.3 Hands-On Tutorial: Spinning Up Multi-Project & Multi-Worktree Concurrency

Here is the complete, copy-pasteable workflow from scratch:

Step 3: Broadcast .env and Local Agent Configs from the Main Repo

Add the following wt-sync shell function to your ~/.zshrc (or keep it as a repo script). Run it after creating new worktrees to propagate critical .gitignored files from the main repository:

Step 4: Launch and Dispatch Agent Tasks inside Worktree Panes

You can either type claude interactively inside a pane or script agent launch and task execution from the CLI:

4.4 Global Status Inspection & Main-Repo Merge Convergence

When multiple worktrees are running in parallel, a traditional IDE sidebar only shows the Git status of a single folder. Drop this 12-line wt-status script into ~/bin/ to inspect uncommitted file counts (dirty) and commit divergence (-behind/+ahead relative to master) across every worktree in a single glance:

Once the agents in your worktrees finish their tasks and light up green (done), converge their work in the main repository and rebase active worktrees onto the updated baseline:

5. Daily Workflow & Agent Self-Orchestration (Fan-out) Tutorial

Distilled into daily muscle memory, the workflow follows six beats:

5.1 Install the herdr Skill to Unlock Self-Orchestration

Export herdr’s built-in orchestration specification as a global Claude Code Skill. Any primary agent running inside a herdr pane will automatically detect its environment (via HERDR_ENV=1 and HERDR_PANE_ID) and know how to invoke the herdr CLI to orchestrate sibling panes:

5.2 Scenario 1: Primary Agent Splits a Right Pane to Spawn a Code Reviewer

When you tell your primary agent, “Once you finish the changes, split a pane to the right and spin up a reviewer agent to audit the current diff,” the primary agent executes these orchestration primitives automatically:

5.3 Scenario 2: Primary Agent Fans Out Three Parallel Workers

For larger tasks that decompose cleanly across modules (such as profiling latency across three microservices or migrating three independent modules across wt-1..3), the primary agent can execute a parallel fan-out script—dispatching all prompts non-blockingly first, then synchronizing on a --wait barrier:

5.4 Multi-Machine Scaling: Attaching Headless Compute Nodes over LAN

If you have an always-on Mac mini or Linux workstation on your LAN, configure passwordless SSH in ~/.ssh/config and run a single command on your primary laptop to merge both machines into one unified sidebar:

Once attached, the remote machine’s Workspaces appear directly in your local sidebar—letting you monitor and control agents across both machines from a single window. Even when you close your laptop lid for the commute, heavy refactoring tasks on the headless workstation continue running at full speed.

6. Architectural Deep Dive: The Three-Tier Orthogonal Agent Stack

As concurrency scales further, terminal split panes alone are insufficient. You must architecturally decouple the Control Plane, Session Layer, and Memory Layer:

Architectural TierPrimary ProviderResponsibility Boundary & Primitives
Control PlaneherdrOwns PTY pane lifecycles, status light sensing (working/blocked/done), process spawning, and prompt/wait/send-keys scheduling. Note: prompt is a blind string pipe—the control plane is deliberately agnostic to domain semantics
Session LayerAgent CLI Native StoragePersists conversation transcripts on disk scoped by project directory (e.g., Claude Code’s -c to continue the latest session, -r to pick a historical session, --fork to branch a conversation). Switching terminal hosts never loses dialogue history
Memory LayerSemantic Memory Store (e.g., OpenViking)Persists cross-session, cross-agent architectural decisions and post-mortems. Any durable memory system supporting “write to an explicit URI → retrieve via semantic search across sessions” can fulfill this tier

Core Layering Discipline: Never pipe massive blocks of context between agents using blind herdr pane send-keys keystrokes. The clean multi-agent contract is: the Control Plane governs where a task runs and whether it has finished; the Session Layer governs where the current dialogue is; and cross-agent knowledge handoff flows strictly through the Memory Layer (workers write structured conclusions to an explicit memory URI or handoff file, and the primary agent reads them by address).

7. After Hours: End-to-End Mobile Remote Takeover

Once a concurrent multi-agent environment is humming along, the next natural question arises: when you step away from your desk for dinner or hop on the subway, who approves the permission prompt when an agent hits blocked?

Remote desktop apps (VNC, TeamViewer, AnyDesk) are most people’s first instinct—and the worst possible mobile experience. Pinch-zooming a 27-inch desktop on a 6-inch phone screen while full-screen TUI redraws blur into compression artifacts is pure friction. Because the target you want to control is a terminal session, the native protocol for the job is SSH.

For a home or office Mac behind NAT without a public IP, I use a lightweight cloud VPS + frp reverse proxy + Termius on iOS/Android + Bark lock-screen push notifications to form a zero-public-exposure remote takeover loop:

This remote pipeline interlocks seamlessly with the herdr environment described above:

  • Zero noise while things work: Your phone stays completely silent while agents are working. Only when a pane triggers permission_prompt (blocked) or finishes a long run (Stop) does the hook script push an instant alert with the project name to your phone’s lock screen;
  • 10-second mobile resolution: Tap the notification, open Termius to connect to your Mac, type herdr to attach to the exact desktop split view, switch to the amber-lit pane to press y, and lock your phone—the agent immediately resumes execution.

📖 Full Deployment Guide: For line-by-line cloud frps and Mac frpc (LaunchAgent auto-healing) configurations, macOS sshd PAM keyboard-interactive hardening, ~/.claude/settings.json mobile push hook scripts, and three critical production pitfalls, read the companion article: Reaching a Private Mac from Anywhere: End-to-End Mobile Remote Control with frp, SSH, and Termius.

8. Production Pitfalls & Troubleshooting Guide

Here is a consolidated troubleshooting checklist distilled from daily production use of herdr:

  1. prefix Keybindings Never Trigger Anything:
    herdr’s prefix key (default Ctrl+B) uses a strict two-stroke sequence—press Ctrl+B and release your fingers completely, then press the action key (such as v, c, or ?). Holding Ctrl+B down while pressing the action key will fail 100% of the time in every terminal emulator.

  2. Lighting Up Status Indicators for Unsupported Agents (e.g., CodeBuddy):
    Take codebuddy as an example: it is absent from herdr 0.9.5’s built-in agent enum, screen-matching manifests, and integration install targets. Moreover, the official docs state that Override manifest rules can only tweak regexes for already-recognized agent kinds—they cannot register a brand-new agent type.
    The official first-class solution is to use the agent’s own lifecycle hooks to call herdr pane report-agent directly:

    Because every herdr pane automatically injects the HERDR_PANE_ID environment variable into child processes, mapping six standard lifecycle events in your agent’s hook config gives you full status light support:

    • SessionStart → --state idle
    • UserPromptSubmit → --state working
    • Stop → --state idle
    • Notification (permission_prompt) → --state blocked
    • Notification (idle_prompt) → --state idle
    • SessionEnd → herdr pane release-agent "$HERDR_PANE_ID"

  3. Two Hidden Traps with herdr machine add:

    • The Default No Prompt Trap: If the remote machine already has a running herdr server, the CLI asks interactively whether to stop and replace it ([y/N]). Pressing Enter accepts the default N, which silently aborts saving the machine registration. You must explicitly type y and press Enter;
    • Daemon Contention: If you previously configured a custom LaunchAgent or systemd unit on the remote machine to keep herdr server alive, it will fight with herdr’s machine replacement logic. Remove custom service wrappers on remote nodes and let herdr’s machine mode manage the server lifecycle natively.

  4. Edge Cases in State Detection & Full-Screen TUI Output Reading:

    • unknown Does Not Mean Finished: An unknown status means the agent process is still running but its current screen state cannot be classified. Run herdr agent explain --json to inspect the exact state-machine evaluation;
    • CLI agent read Does Not Clear the done Light: Only focusing the pane interactively inside the TUI client transitions an agent from done back to idle;
    • Alternate Screen Buffer Truncation: Full-screen TUI agents like Claude Code render inside the terminal’s Alternate Screen buffer. Long responses do not scroll into the standard terminal scrollback buffer, meaning herdr agent read only captures the visible tail on screen. When scripting automated fan-out workflows, always instruct worker agents in their prompt to write full reports to a designated Markdown or JSON file, and have the primary agent read the file from disk rather than scraping the pane.

  5. Logs & Hot-Reload Entry Points:

    • Runtime log files: ~/.config/herdr/herdr*.log
    • Check client/server health and versions: herdr status (or herdr status server / herdr status client)
    • Dump the complete default configuration reference: herdr --default-config
    • After editing ~/.config/herdr/config.toml, run herdr server reload-config to apply changes in milliseconds without restarting the server.

9. Command Cheat Sheet

entry.title: herdr × Git Worktree：多 Agent 并发开发环境实践
entry.content:
💡 Read English Version (英文版)

并发跑多个 Coding Agent 时，难点不在“把它们跑起来”，而在三件事：文件互踩、状态盲区、会话脆弱。本文从 git worktree 和 herdr 两块地基讲起，给出我实际在用的项目级并发开发环境设计：一个仓库多份 worktree、Agent 按任务现场指定、主仓统一合并收口。环境基于 herdr 0.9.5 / macOS，核心概念与命令跨平台通用。

1. 多 Agent 并发的三堵墙

当你同时开启 5 个终端窗口并发跑 Coding Agent 时，很快就会陷入“打地鼠”式的混乱：A 窗口的 Agent 正在改公共模块，B 窗口的 Agent 顺手把同一个文件覆盖了；C 窗口的 Agent 卡在危险命令权限确认弹窗上静默等了半小时，你直到切过去才发现；更致命的是手滑关掉一个终端窗口，跑了一半的重构连同上下文当场灰飞烟灭。

把这些痛点拆开，背后是三堵基础设施之墙：

问题典型现象底层根因
文件互踩两个 Agent 同时改一个仓库，A 改到一半被 B 覆盖或触发构建报错多个并发进程共享同一个物理工作目录（Working Tree）
状态盲区谁在思考、谁卡在权限确认、谁已跑完，只能挨个切窗口肉眼轮询传统终端复用器只管转发 PTY 字节流，不认识窗格里跑的是 Agent
会话脆弱终端窗口误关或 SSH 闪断 = Agent 进程收到 SIGHUP 死亡，现场全没Agent 进程直接挂在前台窗口的 PTY 会话上，缺乏后台守护层

解法不需要重造轮子，两块现成工具分层补齐：git worktree 管物理文件隔离，herdr 管 Agent 状态感知与后台会话存活。把它们按一套严密的工程纪律组合起来，就是完整的多 Agent 并发开发环境。

2. 地基一：Git Worktree——一个仓库，多个工作树

2.1 它解决什么问题

让两个 Agent 并发修改同一个代码仓库，常见的三种土办法都有明显代价：

  • Clone 多份独立仓库：磁盘占用翻倍，本地提交互不可见，分支同步必须绕道远端 origin 中转；
  • 同目录来回 git checkout：天然串行，根本无法并发；
  • Stash 舞蹈：git stash → 切分支 → 修改 → git stash pop，冲突概率随并发数指数级上升。

git worktree 是 Git 官方给出的标准答案：同一个 .git 对象库，挂载多个独立的工作目录（Checkout）。每份工作树拥有独立的物理目录和当前分支，但底层共享同一个 .git/objects 与引用库——任何一份工作树里 git commit 的代码，其他工作树在同一秒内即可直接看见、直接 merge 或 rebase，零网络同步成本。

2.2 高频命令速览

2.3 两条铁律

  1. Worktree 内只 commit，严禁 push：各工作树只负责在自己的任务分支上往前推进本地提交；合并与远端推送统一回到主仓库执行。若允许多个工作树各自向远端乱 push，远端分支历史与 CI 流水线会迅速陷入互相踩踏。
  2. 合并统一在主仓收口：在主仓库（固定停留在 master/main）逐条执行 git merge --no-edit <branch>；遇到冲突在主仓统一裁决，保留双方有效改动，严禁在工作树里用 --ours / --theirs 一刀切抹掉他人代码。

2.4 必踩的第一坑：gitignored 文件不会自动跟过来

.env 环境变量、本地私钥、未入库的 Agent 本地配置（如 .claude/settings.local.json）这类被 .gitignore 忽略的文件，在新 worktree 检出后默认不存在。如果不处理，新工作树里的项目一跑就会因为缺环境变量或丢 MCP 配置而报错。后文 §4.3 会给出主仓一键广播脚本的落地解法。

3. 地基二：herdr——认识 Agent 的终端复用器

3.1 核心定位

herdr 是一个用 Rust 编写的专为 AI Agent 设计的单二进制终端多路复用器。与传统仅转发字节流的终端工具不同，它做对了一件关键的事——原生理解窗格（Pane）里跑的是不是 Coding Agent，以及这个 Agent 当前处于什么生命周期状态。

它的底层采用 C/S 架构：后台 herdr server 守护进程持有所有窗格的 PTY 文件描述符，前台 TUI 只是附着（Attach）上去的渲染视图。这是它一切持久化能力的根源：前台终端窗口随时可以关掉，Agent 进程始终稳稳活在后台 server 里。

3.2 核心概念模型

概念工程含义
server后台守护进程，持有本机全部 PTY 会话；一个 server 可同时挂载任意多个代码仓库
workspace项目级容器，通常一个 Git 仓库对应一个 workspace；与你在哪个目录敲 herdr 无关
pane终端窗格；既可以跑普通交互式 Shell，也可以托管各类 Coding Agent
agent被 herdr 识别并追踪的 Agent 进程，通过 --kind 指定类型（claude / codex / pi / opencode / antigravity-cli 等，0.9.5 版本共内置 24 种）
stateAgent 的实时生命周期状态：working / blocked / idle / done

3.3 三层递进价值

  1. 会话持久化（底座价值）：MacBook 合盖休眠、SSH 网络闪断、手滑关掉终端窗口，后台 Agent 任务照常运行，重连后敲 herdr 一秒恢复完整分屏现场。
  2. 全局状态看板（核心差异化价值）：左侧边栏实时渲染每个项目、每个窗格内 Agent 的状态灯（尤其是黄灯 blocked 与绿灯 done），彻底消灭切窗口轮询的心智负担。
  3. Agent 自编排（高阶涌现价值）：为 Agent 注入官方 herdr Skill 后，窗格里的主 Agent 可以自己调用 CLI 分屏、拉起子 Agent、派发子任务、阻塞等待完成并读取产出——这是传统终端脚本极难做到的闭环。

避坑认知：不要把 herdr 单纯当成“多 worktree 启动器 + 完成提醒工具”。Worktree 隔离只是按需开启的辅助能力，上面三层价值才是主体；而且如果跳过 herdr integration install 步骤，状态识别会退化为脆弱的“屏幕文本正则猜测”，准确率大打折扣。

3.4 安装部署与状态上报接入

在 macOS 上通过 Homebrew 即可一键安装，随后务必为你常用的 Agent CLI 安装官方 Integration 插件：

herdr integration install 的本质是向对应 Agent 的全局配置（例如 ~/.claude/settings.json 的 hooks 字段）注入轻量级回调命令。每当 Agent 开始执行、弹出权限确认或结束回合时，都会通过本地 IPC 毫秒级通知 herdr server，让 blocked 和 done 的判定达到 100% 准确。

3.5 交互方式与核心键位

herdr 采用鼠标一等公民设计：点击切换窗格焦点、拖拽分割线调整大小、右键呼出窗格操作菜单、鼠标拖选直接复制文本，全程无需记键位即可流畅操作。

键盘操作则沿用经典的 Prefix 模式（默认前缀键为 Ctrl+B——注意是先按一下 Ctrl+B 松开，再按后续动作键，而非一直按住）：

快捷键作用说明
prefix + v向右垂直分屏（新建右侧窗格）
prefix + -向下水平分屏（新建下方窗格）
prefix + c在当前 Workspace 内新建 Tab
prefix + Shift+G交互式新建 Git Worktree
prefix + ?弹出实时快捷键全集浮层
prefix + qDetach 脱离当前视图（后台任务继续运行；直接关终端窗口效果相同）

持久化体感：随时按 prefix + q 或直接 Cmd+W 关掉终端窗口 → 在任意目录重新输入 herdr 即可无损附着回原现场。只有显式执行 herdr server stop 才会真正终止后台守护进程与所有窗格。

3.6 状态灯语义与注意力转变

状态灯生命周期含义你的响应策略
working正在思考、推理或执行工具调用忽略，让它自己跑
blocked卡在危险操作权限审批或交互式提问，等你按键立即切过去处理（最高优先级）
idle回合已结束且你已查看过现场，处于待命状态可随时派发下一个任务
done任务刚刚跑完，且你还没有切过去看过结果（聚焦该窗格后自动归为 idle）抽空切过去验收成果

这套状态机直接重塑了日常开发心流：你可以同时在三四个项目里挂着 Agent 跑任务，自己专心写核心设计或看文档；眼角余光扫一眼侧边栏——平时全当它们不存在，只在亮起 blocked 或 done 时介入。

3.7 宿主终端选型与配置：为什么定案 Tabby

herdr 本身是跑在终端模拟器里的 TUI 程序，宿主终端（Host Terminal）的事件透传能力直接决定了日常操作顺不顺手。

在我的高频工作流里，有两条不可妥协的硬指标：

  1. 全鼠标右键管理窗格：分屏、关闭、缩放（Zoom）全部走鼠标右键菜单；
  2. Cmd+V 剪贴板直贴图片：把报错截图、架构草图直接 Cmd+V 粘贴进 Claude Code 等多模态 Agent。

围绕这两条硬指标实测主流 macOS 终端后，结论非常明确：

宿主终端Cmd+V 贴图进 herdr 内 Agent鼠标右键与特性支持实测结论
Tabby (Electron)全链路畅通（粘贴在应用层消化，不被 PTY 吞掉）关闭应用层右键菜单后，100% 透传给 herdr主力定案（零损失）
Ghostty断裂（Cmd+V 只送达裸字符 "v"，无论是否经 herdr 均贴不了图）原生支持 Kitty 键盘协议与鼠标透传贴图刚需下一票否决
Warp受限于自有输入框模型Block 输入模型劫持鼠标与按键事件，与 TUI 复用器冲突不兼容
macOS Terminal.app不支持富媒体剪贴板透传缺乏 Kitty Keyboard Protocol，修饰键残缺不推荐

Tabby 零摩擦配置三步走：

  1. 打开 Tabby Settings → Application，找到 “Show menu on right click” 并将其关闭（对应配置文件中的 rightClick: 'off'）。关闭后，在窗格内点击右键将直接呼出 herdr 原生分屏菜单；
  2. 字体与主题推荐：Maple Mono NF CN 搭配 Catppuccin Mocha 配色；
  3. 给纯键盘流用户的补充建议：如果你不依赖 Cmd+V 贴图、而是重度依赖复杂键盘快捷键，宿主终端需满足三项条件——原生鼠标事件透传、支持 Kitty Keyboard Protocol（建议 Kitty ≥ 0.33 或 Alacritty ≥ 0.15.0，旧版 Alacritty 存在按键 release 字节重复发送 Bug）、以及在终端设置中开启 Option as Meta。

4. 组合实战：项目级并发环境设计

4.1 目录与会话拓扑

把 git worktree 和 herdr 拼在一起后，单个项目在磁盘与内存中的标准拓扑如下：

全局只有一个 herdr server，左侧边栏挂载你手头的全部项目（每个仓库一个 Workspace）以及每个项目下正在并发推进的 Worktree 窗格，一块屏幕掌握所有 Agent 的冷暖。

4.2 五条工程设计原则

  1. Workspace 绑项目，绝不绑 Agent：一个 Git 仓库对应一个 Workspace；多项目并行就是多个 Workspace 并存，彼此隔离。
  2. Worktree 只为并发隔离而生：单 Agent 改单个项目时直接在主仓跑即可，完全用不上 worktree；只有当两个以上 Agent 需要同时修改同一个仓库时才开辟 worktree。

    反面教训：我早期曾按 Agent 种类建目录（比如 myproject-claude、myproject-opencode），结果一旦想在第二个目录里换用 Claude，目录命名就和实际跑的 Agent 错位了。正确认知是：目录只代表“仓库的第 N 号隔离副本（wt-1、wt-2）”，与谁在里面干活毫无关系。

  3. Agent 现场按需指定，目录编号不编码用途：wt-1 只是槽位序号；窗格里今天跑 claude 写功能、明天跑 codex 修 Bug、后天跑 opencode 写测试，全由启动时的命令或 --kind 参数现场决定，目录原地不动。
  4. 主仓只做收口与基线维护：所有 worktree 内部只允许 git commit，严禁执行 git push；分支合并、冲突裁决与远端推送统一回到主仓执行（将 §2.3 铁律固化为环境级约束）。
  5. 未追踪配置从主仓单向广播：.env、本地密钥、MCP 配置等 gitignored 文件以主仓为唯一事实源（SSOT），通过同步脚本一键分发到各 worktree 槽位，彻底填平 §2.4 的坑。

4.3 实战教程：从零拉起多项目与多 Worktree 并发单元

第三步：从主仓一键广播 .env 与本地 Agent 配置

4.4 全局状态巡检与主仓合并收口

多个 worktree 并发跑起来后，传统的 IDE 侧边栏只能看一个目录的 Git 状态。准备一个十来行的 wt-status 脚本放进 ~/bin/，即可在主仓一屏巡检所有分支的未提交改动（dirty）与落后/领先主干的提交数（-behind/+ahead）：

5. 日常工作流与 Agent 自编排（Fan-out）教程

把上述动作浓缩成每日肌肉记忆，就是下面六个节拍：

5.1 安装 herdr Skill 解锁 Agent 自编排

只要把 herdr 内置的编排说明导出为 Claude Code 的全局 Skill，跑在 herdr 窗格里的主 Agent 就会自动意识到自己身处 herdr 环境中（通过 HERDR_ENV=1 与 HERDR_PANE_ID 环境变量），并学会自己调用 herdr CLI 操控其他窗格：

5.2 场景一：主 Agent 自动分屏拉起 Reviewer 交叉审校

当你对主 Agent 说“改完后开个右分屏拉一个 reviewer 帮我审一下当前 diff”，主 Agent 会在后台自动执行以下编排原语：

5.3 场景二：主 Agent 并发扇出（Fan-out）三个 Worker 并行攻关

遇到需要同时拆解多模块的大任务（例如同时排查 3 个微服务的接口耗时，或在 3 个 worktree 中并行编写互不重叠的模块），可以直接执行并行扇出脚本——先非阻塞派发全部任务，再统一 --wait 屏障同步：

5.4 跨机扩展：局域网无头算力节点接入

如果手头有一台常驻开机的 Mac mini 或 Linux 工作站，只需配好 ~/.ssh/config 免密登录别名，在主力机上执行一行命令即可将其纳入同一个侧边栏：

接入后，本地侧边栏会直接出现远端机器的 Workspace 分组——一个窗口同时掌控两台机器上的全部 Agent；即使把主力笔记本合盖塞进背包，远端机器上的重构任务依然全速推进。

6. 进阶视角：多 Agent 协作的三层正交架构

当并发规模继续扩大时，只靠终端分屏还不够，必须在架构上把控制面、会话层、记忆层彻底解耦：

架构分层核心承担者职责边界与工程原语
控制面 (Control Plane)herdr负责窗格 PTY 生命周期、状态灯感知（working/blocked/done）、进程拉起与 prompt/wait/send-keys 调度。注意：prompt 只是盲传字符串，控制面不理解业务语义
会话层 (Session Layer)各 Agent CLI 自持对话上下文按项目目录持久化落盘（如 Claude Code 的 -c 续接最近会话、-r 挑选历史会话、--fork 分叉推演）。换终端宿主绝不丢失对话历史
记忆层 (Memory Layer)语义记忆库（如 OpenViking）负责跨会话、跨 Agent 的长期架构决策与踩坑结论沉淀。任何支持**“写入明确 URI 地址 → 跨会话语义检索取回”**的持久记忆系统都可承担此层

核心分层纪律：严禁通过 herdr pane send-keys 在不同 Agent 之间盲传大段上下文文本。正确的协作范式是：控制面只管“活儿在哪个窗格跑、跑完没有”，会话层管“当前任务聊到哪一步了”，而跨 Agent 的知识交接一律走记忆层（Worker 将结论写入明确的记忆 URI 或交接文件，主 Agent 按地址精准读取）。

7. 下班之后：手机远程接管全链路

多 Agent 并发环境跑顺之后的下一个自然诉求是：人离开工位去吃晚饭或在地铁上时，卡在 blocked 权限确认弹窗上的 Agent 谁来点确认？

很多人的第一反应是向日葵、ToDesk 或 VNC 远程桌面——但在 6 寸手机屏幕上缩放拖拽 27 寸桌面、看着全屏 TUI 重绘糊成马赛克，是效率最低的折磨。既然我们要操控的对象本质上是终端会话，最优雅的方式就是回归终端的原生协议：SSH。

针对家庭或办公室内网 Mac 没有公网 IP 的场景，我用一台轻量云 VPS + frp 反向代理 + 手机端 Termius + Bark 锁屏推送，搭起了一套零公网暴露面的远程接管闭环：

这套方案与本文的 herdr 环境天然咬合：

  • 平时手机完全静默：只有当某个窗格里的 Agent 触发 permission_prompt 变为 blocked、或长任务跑完触发 Stop 时，Hooks 脚本才会给手机发一条带项目名的锁屏通知；
  • 掏出手机 10 秒处理：点开 Termius 连上内网 Mac，敲 herdr 瞬间附着回桌面上的完整并发视图，用虚拟方向键切到黄灯窗格按 y 放行，锁屏揣回兜里，Agent 继续往下跑。

📖 完整部署指南：关于云端 frps 与 Mac 侧 frpc（LaunchAgent 开机自愈）的逐行配置、macOS sshd 禁用 PAM 键盘交互认证的安全加固、~/.claude/settings.json 锁屏推送脚本，以及实测必踩的三个大坑，请直接阅读姊妹篇《外网连进内网 Mac：frp + SSH + Termius 手机远程全链路实战》。

8. 实战踩坑与排查指南

最后把日常高频使用 herdr 过程中提炼出的关键排障经验整理成清单，供碰到同类症状时按图索骥：

  1. prefix 快捷键怎么按都没反应：
    herdr 的前缀键（默认 Ctrl+B）采用严格的两段式触发——先按下 Ctrl+B 并完全松开手指，再按后续动作键（如 v、c、?）。如果习惯性一直按住 Ctrl+B 不放再去按动作键，在任何终端里都会100% 失败。

  2. 使用尚未内置的 Agent（如 CodeBuddy）时如何点亮状态灯：
    以 codebuddy 为例，herdr 0.9.5 的内置枚举、屏幕正则清单与 integration install 列表里都没有它；且官方文档明确说明 Override manifest 只能微调已内置 Agent 的匹配规则，无法凭空注册新 Agent 类型。
    正解是直接走官方一等公民路径——利用 Agent 自身的 Hooks 调用 herdr pane report-agent 主动上报：

    因为 herdr 窗格会自动向子进程注入 HERDR_PANE_ID 环境变量，只需在 Agent 的配置文件中将 6 个标准生命周期事件映射到上述命令即可完美点亮状态灯：

    • SessionStart → --state idle
    • UserPromptSubmit → --state working
    • Stop → --state idle
    • Notification (permission_prompt) → --state blocked
    • Notification (idle_prompt) → --state idle
    • SessionEnd → herdr pane release-agent "$HERDR_PANE_ID"

  3. herdr machine add 接入远端机器的两个暗坑：

    • 默认选项陷阱：当远端机器已有运行中的 herdr server 时，CLI 会交互式提问“是否停掉并替换远端 server？ [y/N]”。注意默认回车是 N（直接放弃保存配置），必须显式输入 y 回车才能完成注册；
    • 守护进程打架：如果远端机器之前自己配过 LaunchAgent 或 systemd 常驻守护 herdr server，在执行替换动作时会发生进程争抢。接入 machine 模式前，应先停掉自定义的守护配置，把 server 生命周期交还给 herdr 自身管理。

  4. 状态判定与全屏 TUI 输出读取的边界：

    • unknown 不代表跑完：状态显示 unknown 说明 Agent 仍在运行但当前屏幕特征无法归类，可执行 herdr agent explain --json 查看底层状态机给出的具体判定依据；
    • CLI agent read 不会消除 done 绿灯：只有人类在 TUI 界面中真正将焦点切入该窗格，done 状态才会归位为 idle；
    • 备用屏（Alternate Screen）截断问题：像 Claude Code 这类全屏 TUI 程序渲染在终端备用屏上，超长回复不会进入普通终端滚动缓冲区（Scrollback Buffer），导致 herdr agent read 只能抓到当前一屏的尾部。在自动化 Fan-out 编排中，务必在 Prompt 里要求子 Agent 将完整分析报告写入指定的 Markdown/JSON 文件，主 Agent 直接读文件而非抓屏幕。

  5. 日常日志与配置热重载入口：

    • 运行日志路径：~/.config/herdr/herdr*.log
    • 查看前后端连接与版本状态：herdr status（或 herdr status server / herdr status client）
    • 导出全量默认配置参考：herdr --default-config
    • 修改 ~/.config/herdr/config.toml 后无需重启 server，执行 herdr server reload-config 即可毫秒级热生效。

9. 常用命令速查卡

entry.title: Remote Access to a Private Mac: Full-Stack Guide with frp, SSH, and Termius
entry.content:
💡 阅读中文原版 (Chinese Version)

Production Baseline: macOS (Apple Silicon) + frp 0.72.0 + Cloud Linux VPS (Debian 12) + Termius (iOS / Android) + herdr persistent session layer.

1. The Problem: You Are Away, Your Mac Is Behind NAT

Your Mac is running workloads you cannot afford to abandon—a long compilation job, local microservices, a dozen concurrent AI coding agent sessions, or a carefully arranged terminal workspace. When you step away from your desk, you have only two choices: head back, or connect remotely.

Most developers instinctively reach for remote desktop tools (RustDesk, TeamViewer, AnyDesk) to stream the Mac screen to their phone. It works in theory, but the mobile experience is miserable: driving a 27-inch desktop on a 6-inch touchscreen means drifting cursors, illegible text, and full-screen TUI redraws that smear into compression artifacts. What you actually need to control is not “the Mac’s screen”—it is those specific terminal sessions. And the native protocol for terminal sessions is SSH.

The obstacle is network topology: a Mac at home or in the office sits behind NAT without a public IPv4 address. How does your phone reach it? This guide walks through a battle-tested setup using a minimal cloud VPS + frp to bridge the NAT gap, paired with Termius and the herdr persistent session layer to connect from anywhere in the world directly into your Mac shell—covering architecture trade-offs, deployment, sshd hardening, push notifications, and three hard-won troubleshooting traps.

2. Architecture Trade-Offs: Why frp + SSH?

Before building this pipeline, I evaluated every viable remote takeover route as of November 2026:

RouteTake Over Existing SessionsMobile Push AlertsEndpoint & Network RealityCost
frp + SSH (This Guide)✅ All sessions (with herdr session layer)✅ DIY (Bark/ntfy)✅ Low-latency direct connection via regional VPS; works with any LLM endpointExisting VPS
Claude Official Remote Control✅ Attach via /remote-control✅ Official APNs❌ Requires claude.ai subscription login + direct connection to api.anthropic.com; incompatible with custom/proxy endpointsMonthly sub
Happy (Open-Source Mobile App)❌ Only sessions launched by Happy✅ APNs⚠️ Custom endpoint passthrough unverifiedFree
Paseo (Open-Source Control Tower)❌ Only sessions managed by Paseo✅ E2E relay✅Free
Web Terminal (ttyd + reverse proxy)✅❌⚠️ Mobile Safari virtual keyboard & selection bugs; view-only in practiceFree
Tailscale + Mosh Client✅❌⚠️ Public DERP relays add high latency unless self-hosting DERPFree
tmate✅❌❌ Public hosted service shut down; requires self-hosting—

Three decisive engineering reasons make frp + SSH + Persistent Session Layer the clear winner:

  1. Universal takeover of already-running sessions. By running a persistent session layer on the Mac (this guide uses herdr, a terminal multiplexer purpose-built for AI coding agents), a background daemon owns every pseudo-terminal (PTY). No matter how many times SSH disconnects, the processes stay alive in place, and re-attaching restores the exact state instantly. Unlike Happy or Paseo—which can only manage sessions they spawn from scratch—this approach works for everything already running on your machine.
  2. Complete endpoint decoupling. Many engineering teams route Claude Code or OpenCode through enterprise LLM gateways or Anthropic-compatible endpoints (such as GLM or Volcengine Ark). Claude’s official Remote Control strictly requires direct authentication against api.anthropic.com with no custom ANTHROPIC_* environment overrides. Because an SSH tunnel operates purely at the transport layer, it is 100% agnostic to which model endpoint your agents use.
  3. Zero marginal cost with an existing VPS. frp is a battle-tested reverse proxy for NAT traversal (80k+ GitHub stars) that runs in a few megabytes of RAM on any entry-level cloud instance.

3. System Architecture: Three Orthogonal Planes

The system is intentionally decoupled into three orthogonal planes, each solving exactly one problem:

  • 1. Tunnel Plane (frp) — Reachability: Because the Mac sits behind NAT without a public IP, frpc on the Mac initiates an outbound persistent connection to frps :7000 on the cloud VPS. Connecting via SSH from your phone to VPS port :6022 transparently forwards traffic to 127.0.0.1:22 on the Mac.
  • 2. Session Plane (herdr) — Continuity: A background server daemon holds the PTY file descriptors for all panes. Whether your phone drops signal in an elevator, switches between Wi-Fi and cellular, or closes the SSH app, your agents keep running; running herdr upon reconnection restores your exact workspace.
  • 3. Notification Plane (Bark / ntfy) — Timely Awareness: When an agent pauses on a permission prompt (blocked) or finishes a task (Stop), a local lifecycle hook fires a curl push notification straight to your phone’s lock screen—eliminating manual status polling.

4. Server Side: Deploying frps on the VPS (~15 Mins)

4.1 Outbound Pre-Check, Installation, and Configuration

If your corporate firewall blocks non-standard outbound ports, change bindPort in frps.toml and serverPort in frpc.toml to 443 or 8443.

SSH into your Linux VPS (linux_amd64, v0.72.0 shown below), download the release binary, and create /etc/frp:

Generate a 48-character random secret via openssl rand -hex 24 and write /etc/frp/frps.toml:

Two non-negotiable security details:

  • auth.token must have high entropy: In frp, the token is a server-wide shared credential. A weak token turns your public VPS into an open relay.
  • allowPorts is a critical guardrail: By default, frps permits authenticated clients to request any remotePort. Locking allowPorts restricts exposure to your single intended port.

4.2 systemd Daemonization and Permission Lockdown

4.3 Aligning Cloud Security Group Rules

In your cloud provider’s console, allow inbound TCP 7000 (frp control plane) and your SSH entry port (6022 in this example). Always check your cloud console’s existing Security Group rules before picking a port number—if your security group already opens a specific port range, pick your allowPorts and remotePort inside that range rather than debugging silent drops later (see §9.3).

5. Mac Side: frpc + Self-Healing LaunchAgent (~15 Mins)

5.1 Installation and Syntax Verification

Install frpc via Homebrew on your Mac and create the configuration directory:

Write ~/.config/frp/frpc.toml:

Restrict file permissions and run the built-in configuration verifier:

5.2 Auto-Start and Auto-Heal via macOS LaunchAgent

Replace <YOUR_MAC_USERNAME> below with your actual macOS username (whoami; on Intel Macs, use /usr/local/bin/frpc instead of /opt/homebrew/bin/frpc) and save it to ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.frpc.plist:

Bootstrap the agent and verify the tunnel registration:

Combining RunAtLoad and KeepAlive ensures frpc starts automatically on reboot and reconnects immediately after network hiccups.

Finally, verify two macOS host prerequisites:

  1. Enable Remote Login (sshd): Open System Settings → General → Sharing → Remote Login and toggle it on.
  2. Prevent System Sleep: System sleep suspends all network interfaces. On an always-on workstation, run sudo pmset -a sleep 0 disablesleep 1.

6. Mobile Side: Termius Setup & Daily Usage Guide (~10 Mins)

The workflow in Termius (the free tier is sufficient) is identical across iOS and Android.

6.1 Generate a Device-Bound Keypair (Private Key Never Leaves Phone)

  1. Open Termius → Keychain → + → Generate Key.
  2. Select Ed25519 and leave the passphrase empty (some mobile terminal overlays struggle with interactive passphrase prompts; rely on device biometric lock instead).
  3. Tap the newly generated key → Copy Public Key.

Send the single-line public key (ssh-ed25519 AAAA...) to your Mac and append it to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys:

Always tag the end of each key line with a device identifier (termius-iphone, termius-android). Generate a separate keypair on each mobile device rather than sharing private keys—if a phone is ever lost, you can revoke its access by deleting that single line.

6.2 Configure the Host and Connect

In Termius, navigate to Hosts → + → New Host:

FieldValue
Address / Hostname203.0.113.10 (Your VPS public IP)
Port6022 (Matches remotePort)
UsernameYour macOS login username
KeySelect the Ed25519 key generated in §6.1

Save and tap to connect—landing directly at your Mac’s zsh prompt without any password prompt confirms that both the NAT tunnel and public-key authentication are working end-to-end.

6.3 Daily Usage Tutorial: Attaching, Approving Prompts, and Detaching Safely

Landing in the shell is just the entry point; your daily mobile workflow revolves around the persistent session layer:

  1. Re-attach to Your Live Workspace in One Command:
    Type herdr and press Enter. All project workspaces, agent panes, and sidebar status indicators appear immediately.
  2. Switching Panes and Approving Agent Permission Prompts on Mobile:
    • Touch Selection: Termius natively forwards terminal mouse events. Tap directly on any split pane to focus it, or tap a red blocked item in the herdr sidebar to jump straight to the agent awaiting confirmation.
    • Approving Tool Calls: Use the ↑ ↓ arrow keys and Enter on the Termius extended keyboard bar above the virtual keyboard to approve Claude Code / OpenCode permission prompts, or use mobile voice dictation to send follow-up instructions.
    • Viewport Adjustment: Rotate your phone to landscape mode when viewing side-by-side panes, and pinch-to-zoom to adjust font size on the fly.
  3. Clean Detach and Drop-Safe Recovery:
    • Clean Detach: Tap CTRL on the Termius accessory bar (it highlights to lock) → tap b (sends prefix Ctrl+b) → tap q (herdr detach key). You return to the outer shell while all panes keep running in the background.
    • Zero-Loss on Hard Disconnects: Even if you swipe Termius closed or lose cellular signal on a train without detaching, nothing is lost—the Mac-side herdr server daemon owns the PTYs. Reconnect and type herdr to resume right where you left off.

For the complete multi-agent architecture running inside those panes, see the companion guide: herdr × Git Worktree: Concurrent Multi-Agent Development Environment in Practice.

7. Hardening sshd: Verify Keys First, Then Disable Passwords

Any port exposed to the public internet will be hit by automated brute-force scanners within minutes. Once you have verified that key-based login works in §6, disable password authentication completely. Never reverse this order—disabling passwords before testing your key will lock you out.

Create /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/100-hardening.conf on your Mac:

Critical macOS Detail: OpenSSH on macOS enables PAM keyboard-interactive authentication (KbdInteractiveAuthentication) by default, which acts as a twin password channel. Setting only PasswordAuthentication no leaves keyboard-interactive wide open to password brute-forcing. Both directives must be set to no:

This configuration only affects the SSH daemon; macOS local login, Touch ID, Apple Watch unlock, and Screen Sharing use separate authentication stacks and remain untouched.

Verify from an external machine that password authentication is completely dead:

8. Completing the Third Plane: Push Alerts to Your Lock Screen

With the tunnel plane (“reachable”) and session plane (“resumable”) in place, the final piece is eliminating manual polling. By wiring Claude Code lifecycle hooks to Bark (iOS) or ntfy (Android / cross-platform), your phone alerts you the instant an agent blocks on a permission prompt or finishes its task.

8.1 Create the Lightweight Notification Script

Create ~/bin/agent-notify on your Mac and make it executable (chmod +x ~/bin/agent-notify):

Run touch ~/.agent-notify-phone before stepping away from your Mac, and rm -f ~/.agent-notify-phone when you return so your phone stays quiet while you are at your desk.

8.2 Wire Up Claude Code Lifecycle Hooks

Add Notification (fired on permission_prompt) and Stop (fired when a turn completes) hooks to ~/.claude/settings.json:

When an agent pauses for approval while you are out, your phone lock screen lights up within one second—tap the banner, open Termius, approve, and lock your phone in under 30 seconds.

9. Field Notes: Three Troubleshooting Traps That Cost an Afternoon

The entire setup takes 30 minutes to configure, yet I spent hours debugging three deceptive failure modes. Every single one reinforces the same engineering rule: when troubleshooting hits a wall, question your measurement tools first.

9.1 Trap 1: Local Port Probes Returning 100% False Positives

  • Misleading Symptom: Running nc -zv <VPS_IP> 6022 from the Mac always returned succeeded! instantaneously—even when frps was stopped—yet actual SSH connections hung and timed out.
  • Root Cause: A proxy client running in TUN mode (Clash / mihomo) was active on the Mac. Its virtual network interface intercepted all outbound TCP SYN packets via fake-ip and completed the TCP handshake locally inside the TUN stack. nc was reporting a local proxy ACK, while zero packets actually left the machine.
  • Takeaway: Never trust port probes (nc, telnet) run from a host with an active TUN proxy. Always verify external reachability from an independent cloud host or a phone on cellular data.

9.2 Trap 2: Silent sshd Timeouts on the VPS Loopback Path

  • Misleading Symptom: To test the tunnel quickly, I ran ssh -p 6022 user@127.0.0.1 directly on the VPS. TCP connected and frp logs showed the proxy forwarding cleanly, but the SSH handshake hung for 4 seconds and died without receiving a single byte of the SSH-2.0-OpenSSH banner—even though nc 127.0.0.1 22 on the Mac returned the banner instantly.
  • Debugging Detour: I ruled out frp version mismatches, TLS settings, work connection pools, and macOS sshd PerSourcePenalties / MaxStartups. I even attached a Python echo server to the exact same tunnel—the echo server responded instantly, while only sshd stayed silent.
  • Root Cause: This was an artifact specific to the VPS self-loopback path (127.0.0.1:6022). The moment I tested from a separate cloud host over the public internet (External Host → VPS Public IP:6022 → Tunnel → Mac sshd), the SSH banner appeared in milliseconds on the first try. I had wasted hours debugging a synthetic loopback path that no real client ever takes.
  • Takeaway: Always test along the exact network path your real client uses.

9.3 Trap 3: The Cloud Security Group Blindspot

  • Misleading Symptom: I picked an arbitrary entry port in frps.toml, verified via ss -tlnp on the VPS that frps was listening, saw start proxy success in frpc.log, and assumed the port was reachable—until an external probe revealed silent packet drops.
  • Root Cause: Cloud Security Groups enforce filtering at the hypervisor boundary outside the guest OS kernel; neither ss nor iptables can see them. Inspect your cloud console’s allowed port ranges before choosing allowPorts and remotePort.

(Bonus macOS note: macOS does not ship with the GNU timeout binary. Writing timeout 5 ssh ... in scripts fails silently; use SSH’s native -o ConnectTimeout=5 flag or install coreutils via Homebrew for gtimeout.)

10. Production Readiness & Security Checklist

Run through these 6 checks in order before calling the deployment production-ready:

  1. VPS Listener Check: ss -tlnp | grep -E '7000|6022' shows both ports in LISTEN state.
  2. Mac Tunnel Check: tail ~/.config/frp/frpc.log shows login to server success and [mac-ssh] start proxy success.
  3. Reboot Self-Heal Check: Reboot the Mac once and verify frpc reconnects automatically via LaunchAgent without manual login.
  4. Mobile Takeover Loop: Put your phone on cellular data → connect via Termius → run herdr → send a message to a live agent and confirm it responds.
  5. Cross-Device Continuity: Detach on mobile (Ctrl+b q), then run herdr on the Mac desktop terminal and verify the session state is intact.
  6. Password Surface Rejection: Run ssh -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -p 6022 <user>@<VPS_IP> true from an external host and confirm Permission denied (publickey).
Control PointImplementationSecurity Objective
frp Authentication48-char token via openssl rand -hex 24Prevent unauthorized clients from using the VPS as a relay
Port WhitelistingallowPorts = [{ single = 6022 }]Prevent clients from binding arbitrary ports on the VPS
Config File Permissionschmod 600 on both frps.toml and frpc.tomlProtect plaintext tokens from local unprivileged processes
SSH Key HygieneEd25519, one keypair per device, comment-taggedPrivate keys never leave devices; instant per-device revocation
Password Channel LockdownPasswordAuthentication no + KbdInteractiveAuthentication noEliminate both password and PAM keyboard-interactive attack surfaces

11. Next-Level Evolution

  • Second Control Surface (Laptop / iPad): Add a 4-line host alias to ~/.ssh/config on any secondary laptop to connect through the same tunnel. If you use herdr, run herdr --remote <ssh-alias> to turn your local terminal into a native thin client attached to the remote Mac’s herdr server.
  • Zero Public Port Exposure (WireGuard / STCP): To hide port 6022 from internet scanners entirely, use frp stcp (Secret TCP) mode for laptop-to-Mac access, or run a lightweight WireGuard hub on the VPS so both your phone and Mac communicate over an encrypted private mesh.

References

  • frp Repository & Documentation: fatedier/frp · gofrp.org
  • herdr (Terminal Multiplexer for AI Agents): herdr.dev · Companion Guide: herdr × Git Worktree: Concurrent Multi-Agent Development Environment in Practice
  • Termius Mobile SSH Client: termius.com
  • Mobile Push Notification Tools: Bark (iOS) · ntfy (Cross-Platform)

entry.title: 外网连进内网 Mac：frp + SSH + Termius 手机远程全链路实战
entry.content:
💡 Read English Version (英文版)

实战基线：macOS（Apple Silicon）+ frp 0.72.0 + 云端 Linux VPS（Debian 12）+ Termius（iOS / Android 双端）+ herdr 常驻会话层。

1. 问题：人在外面，Mac 在家里

那台 Mac 上跑着你想随时回去的东西——编译到一半的任务、一组开发服务、十几个并发运行的 AI coding agent 会话，或者就是一个不想中断的终端环境。人在外面时选择只有两个：回去，或者远程。

多数人的第一反应是远程桌面（ToDesk / 向日葵 / RustDesk），在手机上看 Mac 屏幕。能用，但体验是灾难级的：用 6 英寸手机屏幕操控 27 英寸桌面，鼠标指针漂移、字小到看不清，终端 TUI 的全屏重绘在视频流压缩下糊成一团。你要操控的根本不是“Mac 的屏幕”，而是“那几个终端会话”——那就该用终端的原生方式解决：SSH。

拦路的是网络现实：家里或办公室的 Mac 蜷在 NAT 后面，没有公网 IP，手机从哪连？本文用一台最低配云 VPS + frp 解决这一跳，配合 Termius 与常驻会话层 herdr 打通“世界任何角落 → 你的 Mac shell”全链路——从选型、部署、加固、通知推送到三个实测排障大坑，全部可复现。

2. 选型：为什么是 frp + SSH

动手前我把市面上的远程接管路线完整过了一遍（2026-11 实测状态）：

路线接管已在跑的存量会话手机主动推送国内网络与端点现实成本
frp + SSH（本文）✅ 一切会话（配 herdr 保活层）✅ 可自接（Bark/ntfy）✅ 国内云 VPS 直连低延迟，任意模型端点可用复用已有 VPS
Claude 官方 Remote Control✅ 会话内 /remote-control 补挂✅ 官方 APNs 推送❌ 硬性要求订阅登录 + 直连 api.anthropic.com，走中转/兼容端点的用户全部不可用月订阅
Happy（开源移动客户端）❌ 只能管它自己新启动的会话✅ APNs⚠️ 第三方兼容端点透传未经官方验证免费
Paseo（开源调度台）❌ 只能管它托管的新会话✅ E2E relay✅免费
网页终端（ttyd + 反代）✅❌⚠️ 移动 Safari 软键盘与选区 bug 多，只够“看一眼”免费
Tailscale + mosh 客户端✅❌⚠️ 官方 DERP 中继全在境外，国内直连需自建 DERP免费
tmate✅❌❌ 官方公共服务已关停，须自建服务端—

最终锁定 frp + SSH + 常驻会话层 的三个决定性理由：

  1. 无差别接管“一切已在跑的存量会话”。Mac 侧配一层常驻会话层（本文选用专为 AI Agent 设计的终端多路复用器 herdr），由后台守护进程持有全部 PTY：SSH 断连多少次，进程原地活着，重连即恢复现场。这条路不挑终端里跑的是什么——编译任务、长服务、Claude Code、OpenCode、任何 shell 全部适用。Happy 与 Paseo 都要求会话从头由它们启动，桌面上跑了一半的存量任务接管不了。
  2. 模型端点完全解耦。国内大量开发者走 Anthropic 兼容中转端点（企业网关、智谱 GLM、火山方舟 Ark 等），而 Claude 官方 Remote Control 硬性要求直连 api.anthropic.com 且不得残留自定义 ANTHROPIC_* 环境变量，中转用户直接出局。SSH 隧道工作在传输层，上层 Agent 走什么 API 端点与它完全正交。
  3. 已有 VPS 即零边际成本。frp 是久经验证的内网穿透方案（GitHub 8 万+ Star），一台最低配云主机即可承载，不引入重型守护进程。

3. 架构：三个正交平面

整套体系拆成三个正交平面，每个平面只解决一件事：

  • ① 隧道平面（frp）——够得着：Mac 在 NAT 后没有公网 IP，由 Mac 上的 frpc 主动向云 VPS 的 frps :7000 拨出建立长连接隧道；手机 SSH 连 VPS 的 :6022 入口端口，流量即被透明转发至 Mac 本机的 127.0.0.1:22。
  • ② 会话平面（herdr）——接得上：后台 server 进程持有所有窗格（pane）的伪终端 PTY。手机进电梯断网、切蜂窝网络或主动退出 App，任务都在 Mac 后台继续跑；重连后敲一行 herdr 立刻回到断线前那一秒。
  • ③ 通知平面（Bark / ntfy）——想起来：当 Agent 卡在权限确认弹窗（blocked）或任务执行完毕（Stop）时，通过本地 Hook 一发 curl 把告警推上手机锁屏，无需隔几分钟掏手机盲查。

4. 服务器端：frps 部署（约 15 分钟）

4.1 出站预检与安装配置

动手前先在 Mac 终端跑一行预检，确认所在内网（尤其是公司办公网）没有封禁目标 VPS 的控制端口出站：

若公司防火墙拦截非标端口出站，直接把下文 frps.toml 的 bindPort 与 frpc.toml 的 serverPort 同步改为 443 或 8443。

登录云 VPS（本文以 Linux amd64 架构、v0.72.0 为例），下载解压二进制并创建配置目录：

在Mac或VPS上用 openssl rand -hex 24 生成一串 48 位强随机密钥，写入 /etc/frp/frps.toml：

两条必须卡死的安全基线：

  • auth.token 必须强随机：frp 的 token 是服务端级共享凭据，弱口令等于把公网 VPS 变成公开跳板机。
  • allowPorts 是最容易漏掉的防线：默认情况下 frps 允许客户端申请绑定任意 remotePort，显式白名单将其锁死在唯一入口端口。

4.2 systemd 常驻与权限收口

写入 /etc/systemd/system/frps.service：

收紧配置文件权限并启动服务：

4.3 云厂商安全组对齐

在云厂商控制台安全组中放行 TCP 7000（frp 控制面）与你的 SSH 入口端口（本文示例 6022）。入口端口选在哪个号段，务必先看一眼云控制台安全组已放行的策略——如果安全组已有现成放行区间，直接把 allowPorts 和后文的 remotePort 选在该区间内，省去排查“服务监听正常但外网连不通”的折腾（详见 §9.3）。

5. Mac 端：frpc + LaunchAgent 自愈常驻（约 15 分钟）

5.1 安装与配置校验

在 Mac 上通过 Homebrew 安装客户端并创建配置目录：

写入 ~/.config/frp/frpc.toml：

收紧权限并执行官方内置语法校验：

5.2 LaunchAgent 开机自启与断线自愈

将下方模板中的 <你的Mac用户名> 替换为实际用户名（可通过 whoami 查看；若使用 Intel 芯片 Mac，将 /opt/homebrew/bin/frpc 改为 /usr/local/bin/frpc），写入 ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.frpc.plist：

加载守护进程并验证隧道建立成功：

RunAtLoad + KeepAlive 保证了开机自动拉起、进程异常退出或网络闪断后自动重连。

最后确认 Mac 的两个系统前提：

  1. 开启 SSH 服务端：系统设置 → 通用 → 共享 → 远程登录 打开（或终端验证 sudo launchctl list | grep sshd）。
  2. 禁止休眠断网：机器休眠会掐断所有网络连接。常驻开发机执行 sudo pmset -a sleep 0 disablesleep 1 保持常醒。

6. 手机端：Termius 配置与日常操控教程（约 10 分钟）

iOS 与 Android 端 Termius（免费版即够用）操作流程完全一致。

6.1 生成设备专属密钥（私钥永不出机）

  1. 打开 Termius → Keychain → + → Generate Key。
  2. 类型选择 Ed25519，Passphrase 留空（部分移动端 TUI 渲染口令提示存在兼容问题，依赖手机锁屏与面容 ID 保护即可）。
  3. 生成后点进该密钥 → Copy Public Key。

将复制出的一行公钥（ssh-ed25519 AAAA...）发到 Mac 上，追加进 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys：

建议在每把公钥末尾加设备标识注释（如 termius-iphone、termius-android）。多台移动设备各自独立生成密钥对，严禁跨设备拷贝私钥，日后丢设备只需在 authorized_keys 中删掉对应那一行即可精准吊销。

6.2 配置主机并首次连接

在 Termius 中进入 Hosts → + → New Host：

配置项填写值
Address / Hostname203.0.113.10（你的 VPS 公网 IP）
Port6022（与 remotePort 一致）
Username你的 Mac 登录用户名
Key选择刚生成的 Ed25519 密钥

保存后点击连接——直接落入 Mac 的 zsh 提示符且全程不弹密码框，即代表隧道与公钥认证全线贯通。

6.3 日常使用教程：接管会话、审批权限与无损脱离

连进 Mac shell 只是第一步，真正的日常操作流围绕常驻会话层展开：

  1. 一键附身回到现场：
    在终端直接输入 herdr 回车，屏幕上所有项目的并发 Agent 窗格与侧边栏状态灯原样呈现。
  2. 在手机上切换窗格与处理 Agent 权限弹窗：
    • 触屏直点：Termius 原生支持终端鼠标协议（Mouse Reporting），手指直接点击目标窗格即可聚焦，点击 herdr 侧边栏标红（blocked）的項目即可切过去看是谁在等确认。
    • 审批弹窗：利用 Termius 键盘上方扩展键条的 ↑ ↓ 方向键与 Enter 键，一秒完成 Claude Code / OpenCode 的工具执行授权，或直接语音输入追发下一条 Prompt。
    • 视野调节：分屏较多时将手机横屏，双指捏合实时缩放字号。
  3. 安全脱离（Detach）与断网恢复：
    • 处理完毕准备收起手机时：点 Termius 扩展键条的 CTRL（高亮锁定）→ 点字母 b（发送前缀键 Ctrl+b）→ 再点 q（herdr 脱离键）。此时退回普通 shell，后台进程毫发无损。
    • 暴力断连零损失：哪怕忘记脱离直接划掉 Termius App、锁屏或进地铁断网，也完全不用担心——PTY 由 Mac 本机的 herdr server 进程持有，下次重连敲 herdr 依然原地续接。

我的日常场景是在 Mac 上用 herdr 同时跑十几个 AI coding agent，手机敲一个 herdr 就能巡检全部窗格——这套多 Agent 并发环境搭建详见姊妹篇《herdr × Git Worktree：多 Agent 并发开发环境实践》。

7. sshd 安全加固：先验钥匙，再关密码

6022 端口一旦暴露在公网，几分钟内就会收到全球扫描器的密码爆破请求。必须在第 6 节确认密钥免密登录成功后，彻底关闭 sshd 的密码认证面（顺序绝不能反，先关密码再配密钥会把自己在外面锁死）。

在 Mac 上创建独立加固配置 /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/100-hardening.conf：

关键细节：macOS 的 OpenSSH 默认启用了 PAM 键盘交互认证（KbdInteractiveAuthentication），它是密码登录的“孪生通道”。如果只写 PasswordAuthentication no，外部攻击者依然能通过 keyboard-interactive 尝试系统密码。两行必须同时设为 no 才算彻底焊死密码面：

这项改动只作用于 SSH 协议通道，对 macOS 本机锁屏密码、Touch ID、Apple Watch 解锁及屏幕共享毫无影响。

最后从任意外部机器执行一次拒绝测试，验证攻击面已彻底收口：

8. 补齐第三平面：Agent 卡权限时主动推送手机锁屏

前面打通了“随时连上去”（隧道平面）和“连上去现场还在”（会话平面）。如果跑着长任务，你肯定不想每隔十分钟打开 Termius 轮询一次——加上 Bark（iOS） 或 ntfy（Android / 跨平台） 推送脚本，就能把工作流变成 “手机锁屏收到提醒 → 点开 Termius 30 秒处理完”。

8.1 编写轻量通知脚本

在 Mac 上创建 ~/bin/agent-notify 并赋予执行权限（chmod +x ~/bin/agent-notify）：

离开座位前敲 touch ~/.agent-notify-phone 开启远程哨兵，回到电脑前 rm -f ~/.agent-notify-phone 切回安静模式。

8.2 挂载到 Claude Code 生命周期 Hook

在 ~/.claude/settings.json 中挂载 Notification（卡在权限审批时触发）与 Stop（当前轮任务跑完时触发）钩子：

配置完成后，只要你在外面且 Agent 弹出权限请求，手机锁屏会在 1 秒内收到通知。

9. 踩坑实录：三个价值一下午的排障大坑

整套配置本身半小时就能跑通，但我实测时多花了好几个小时，全折在下面三个极具迷惑性的假象里。它们共同指向一条底层排障铁律：当排障陷入死胡同时，先怀疑自己的观测手段。

9.1 坑一：本机测公网端口，全是假阳性

  • 失真现象：在 Mac 本机执行 nc -zv <VPS_IP> 6022 探测远端端口，无论 VPS 上 frps 是否启动，永远秒回 Connection to ... 6022 port [tcp/*] succeeded!，但真正发起 SSH 连接却立刻卡死。
  • 底层根因：Mac 上开着代理工具的 TUN 模式（Clash / mihomo 系），虚拟网卡通过 fake-ip 与透明劫持接管了全部出站 TCP SYN 包——三次握手在本地内核就被 TUN 协议栈直接 ACK 了，nc 看到的“连接成功”只是本机代理栈回的假象，数据包甚至还没走出网卡。
  • 正确验证姿势：开启了 TUN 代理的主机上，一切 nc / telnet 端口连通性探测结果均不可信。外部可达性测试必须从一台干净的外部云主机发起，或直接用切到 4G/5G 蜂窝网络的手机 Termius 实测。

9.2 坑二：VPS 回环路径上的 sshd 静默超时

  • 失真现象：为了快速验证隧道，我登录到 VPS 上执行 ssh -p 6022 user@127.0.0.1（本机连本机转发口）。结果 TCP 握手秒通、frps/frpc 日志显示代理通道已建立，但 SSH 握手挂起 4 秒后超时断开，连一个字节的 SSH-2.0-OpenSSH Banner 都收不到。同时刻在 Mac 本机测 nc 127.0.0.1 22 却秒回 Banner。
  • 排查弯路：先后怀疑并逐一排除了 frp 版本差异、TLS 加密开关、连接池耗尽、macOS sshd 源地址惩罚（PerSourcePenalties）与 MaxStartups 限制；甚至在 Mac 上临时起了个 Python 回声服务挂进同一条隧道对照——回声服务秒通，唯独 sshd 静默。
  • 底层真相：这是 VPS 本机回环路径（Loopback）特有的边界现象。当我换用另一台外部云主机从公网连 <VPS公网IP>:6022 时，第一次尝试就毫秒级弹出 SSH Banner 并成功登录。我在“服务器上自己连自己”这条真实用户永远不会走的路径上白白消耗了几个小时。
  • 正确验证姿势：测试路径必须 1:1 复刻真实客户端路径。真实流量从外部公网网卡进来，验证就必须从外部公网发起。

9.3 坑三：云安全组的“隐形墙”

  • 失真现象：在 frps.toml 里随手挑了个端口，VPS 上跑 ss -tlnp 看到 frps 正常监听，frpc.log 也打印 start proxy success，便想当然认为公网已经通了——直到从外部云主机探测才发现 SYN 包被静默丢弃。
  • 底层根因：云主机的安全组（Security Group）工作在宿主机虚拟化层，位于 Linux 内核 iptables / nftables 与 ss 视野之外。部署前先去云控制台确认已放行的端口区间，让 allowPorts 与 remotePort 向安全组对齐，能直接省掉一整轮抓包排障。

(附注：macOS 默认没有 GNU timeout 命令，写自动化探测脚本时若用 timeout 5 ssh ... 会因找不到命令静默失败；可用 ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 原生参数替代，或 brew install coreutils 后用 gtimeout。)

10. 生产验收与安全核对清单

上线前按序过一遍以下 6 项，全绿即可长期免维护运行：

  1. VPS 监听检查：ss -tlnp | grep -E '7000|6022' 确认控制面与入口端口均处于 LISTEN。
  2. Mac 隧道检查：tail ~/.config/frp/frpc.log 确认出现 login to server success 与 [mac-ssh] start proxy success。
  3. 重启自愈验证：重启一次 Mac，不人工干预，确认 frpc 由 LaunchAgent 自动拉起并重连 VPS。
  4. 手机接管闭环：手机切蜂窝网络 → Termius 免密连入 → 敲 herdr → 给正在运行的 Agent 发送一条指令并确认响应。
  5. 双端会话同步：手机 Ctrl+b q 脱离后，在 Mac 桌面终端敲 herdr 确认同一现场无缝衔接。
  6. 密码爆破免疫验证：从外部机器执行 ssh -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -p 6022 <用户>@<VPS_IP> true，确认返回 Permission denied (publickey)。
安全控制项落地措施核心防御目标
frp 鉴权凭据openssl rand -hex 24 生成 48 位随机串防止弱口令导致 VPS 沦为公共跳板
端口绑定范围allowPorts = [{ single = 6022 }]阻止客户端越权在 VPS 上暴露额外端口
配置文件权限服务端与客户端均执行 chmod 600 *.toml防止本机非授权进程读取明文 token
SSH 密钥策略Ed25519 算法，一机一钥，行尾标注设备名私钥永不出手机，设备丢失可按行精准吊销
密码通道焊死PasswordAuthentication no + KbdInteractiveAuthentication no彻底消除公网端口被字典爆破的可能

11. 演进方向

  • 第二操控面（笔记本 / iPad 远程接管）：在随身轻薄本上只需加 4 行 ~/.ssh/config 别名即可同样穿透接入；如果 Mac 跑的是 herdr，还可以直接运行 herdr --remote <ssh别名>，把本地终端变成远端 Mac herdr server 的原生瘦客户端。
  • 更强网络隔离（WireGuard / STCP）：若希望连 6022 端口都不对公网扫描器暴露，桌面端之间可切换为 frp stcp（Secret TCP）模式；含手机端接入时可在 VPS 上额外部署 WireGuard 组网，将 SSH 入口完全收入虚拟私网内部。

参考资料

  • frp 官方仓库与文档：fatedier/frp · gofrp.org
  • herdr（AI Agent 终端多路复用器）：herdr.dev · 姊妹篇《herdr × Git Worktree：多 Agent 并发开发环境实践》
  • Termius 移动 SSH 客户端：termius.com
  • 移动端推送工具：Bark (iOS) · ntfy (跨平台)

entry.title: Multi-Agent Git Worktree Collaboration and Environment Isolation: A Practical Tutorial
entry.content:
💡 阅读中文原版 (Chinese Version)

1. Prerequisites and Worktree Slot Agent Selection Criteria

To introduce an AI Agent tool into an isolated Git Worktree slot, you must first evaluate whether it is technically capable of serving as a physically isolated workstation.

1.1 Four Hard Requirements for Slot Eligibility

An Agent qualified to occupy an independent Worktree slot must satisfy all four of the following criteria simultaneously:

  1. Full Code CLI / command-line interaction capability:
    • Must be able to launch a CLI process at a designated Worktree path, with the full ability to autonomously read files, modify code, execute terminal commands, and manage session context.
  2. Authentication-free / seamless skip of web login:
    • Must support direct launch via local configuration files (e.g., .claude/settings.*.json, .opencode/opencode.jsonc), environment variables, or API tokens, without requiring browser-based OAuth interaction or manual login clicks.
  3. Custom API endpoint and subscription support:
    • Must allow developers to flexibly configure BaseURL, custom API keys, or map to enterprise/personal third-party subscriptions (e.g., Ark, GLM, Claude/OpenAI-compatible endpoints), without being locked into a single commercial platform account.
  4. API compatibility range (the decisive criterion):
    • Merely “exposing a base_url configuration field” does not equal true third-party endpoint compatibility — what actually determines whether third-party endpoints can be connected is whether the CLI’s Provider layer is compatible with both the Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Chat Completions API specifications. The slot Agent’s Provider layer must be compatible with both API specifications simultaneously; otherwise, you fall into the trap of “appearing to support custom endpoints while being API-spec-locked” (canonical counterexample: Codex CLI, see 1.2). See the root-cause matrix in 1.2.1.

1.2 Mainstream Agent Tool Worktree Slot Compatibility Analysis

Based on CLI completeness, authentication-free operation, custom endpoint support, and API compatibility range (verified against official documentation and source code as of 2026-08), the verdict is as follows:

TierTools
🟢 Fully Compatible (Recommended for Worktree slots)Claude Code, OpenCode, Crush, Qwen Code, oh-my-pi
🟡 Conditionally Compatible (Depends on API compatibility range and testing)Aider, Copilot CLI, Trae agent, CodeBuddy, Kilo Code
🔴 Not Compatible (API-spec-locked or account-bound)Codex, Gemini, Cursor/Amp, ZCode, iFlow, Comate, CodeGeeX/Doubao MarsCode/iFlyCode, Antigravity CLI (agy), Continue, Antigravity/Trae/Cursor/Windsurf and other GUI-IDE-type agents

1.2.1 Root Cause: API Compatibility Range Determines Endpoint Access

Among the four hard requirements, the granularity of criterion #3 — “custom endpoints” — is the deciding factor. Whether third-party endpoints can be connected fundamentally depends on whether the CLI’s Provider layer is compatible with both the Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Chat Completions API specifications, not on whether a base_url configuration field exists. Codex CLI is the canonical counterexample: it supports custom base_url, yet its Provider layer only implements the Responses API, making it incompatible with virtually all mainstream third-party endpoints.

Provider Compatibility RangeRepresentative CLICompatible Endpoints
Dual-Spec CompatibleClaude Code / OpenCode / Crush / Qwen Code / Kilo CodeArk Anthropic endpoint + GLM OpenAI endpoint, both sides ✅
OpenAI Chat CompletionsAider / GitHub Copilot CLIOpenAI-compatible endpoints only (GLM ✅; Ark requires OpenAI-compatible mode)
OpenAI Responses APICodex CLINo mainstream third-party endpoint implements this API ❌
Gemini proprietaryGemini CLIGoogle-only ❌

Selection Iron Law: Only “dual-spec compatible” CLI tools qualify as truly flexible persistent slots. When evaluating any new CLI, first check whether its Provider layer is compatible with both the Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Chat Completions API specifications — otherwise, you will repeat the Codex misjudgment of “appearing to support custom endpoints while being API-spec-locked.”

2. Overview and Core Concepts

2.1 Basic Work Environment: One Main GUI Agent + Multiple CLI Agents

The work environment described in this tutorial follows a two-tier architecture:

  • Main GUI Agent (1 instance, orchestrator): A graphical IDE-type Agent (e.g., Trae / Antigravity / Cursor) running in the repository’s main workspace (master branch). Responsible for architecture planning, global visualization, task scheduling, final merge review, and unified git push. It does not directly participate in concurrent detail-level coding.
  • CLI Agents (N instances, concurrent): Command-line Agents (e.g., Claude Code / OpenCode; see 1.2 for the full selection) launched in their respective Git Worktree directories. Each CLI Agent exclusively occupies one Worktree slot and branch, executes specific tasks concurrently, performs local commit, and is strictly forbidden from push.

Operating Model: You sit in front of the main GUI Agent as the orchestrator and scheduler; simultaneously, you open multiple terminals, each entering a different Worktree directory, and launch different CLI Agents to work concurrently. The main workspace and all Worktrees share the same underlying .git repository (branches, history, and tags are globally connected), but the working directories are physically isolated and do not interfere with each other.

2.2 Why Physical Worktree Isolation Is Necessary

Traditional single-workspace branch switching suffers from three fatal pain points under multi-agent concurrency:

  1. Workspace conflicts: Different Agents overwrite each other’s uncommitted local changes or lock files.
  2. Context pollution: Different Agents share the same session context, leading to prompt and context entanglement.
  3. Configuration and skill mutual exclusion: Different Agents invoke different models, MCP services, skill systems, and API endpoints, making it impossible to share a single set of configuration files.

The solution is the Git Worktree + Persistent Slot Branch + Automated Baseline Synchronization architecture: the main GUI Agent guards master, while each CLI Agent occupies a persistent Worktree slot to work independently. Upon completion, the main workspace performs unified merge and baseline synchronization.

Fundamental Assessment: What Worktree Does and Does Not Isolate

  • Worktree isolates: terminal runtime state, build caches, uncommitted dirty code, and slot-private configuration (.claude/ / .opencode/).
  • Worktree does NOT isolate: textual merge conflicts on the same file. If different Agents modify different files, Git auto-merges seamlessly — Worktree isn’t even strictly necessary. If different Agents modify the same file, Worktree merely defers the textual conflict to the moment git merge is executed on master. The ultimate resolution of conflicts therefore depends on the main workspace’s lossless merge mechanism (see Section 6.2).

3. Git Worktree Setup and Persistent Slot Configuration

3.1 Creating Persistent Worktree Slots

In the main workspace root directory (project, opened by the orchestrator tool or terminal), allocate independent directory slots and Git branches for CLI-capable assisting Agents:

3.2 Slot Red Lines and Management Discipline

  • Physically forbid delete / rm: project-claude and project-opencode are persistent workstations; physically deleting the Worktree or its branch is strictly forbidden.
  • Physically forbid push: All child slots are only responsible for local development and commit; git push is exclusively executed by the main workspace (master) after merge completion.

4. Agent Differentiated Environment Isolation (Models / MCP / Skill / Spec / Endpoints)

For each CLI Agent to operate independently in its own slot, the environment and configuration files must be isolated and assembled.

4.1 Slot CLI Agent Workstation Initialization and Environment Assembly

When launching a CLI Agent in each Worktree slot, five configuration layers — «Discipline → Enforcement → Capability → Endpoint → Retrieval» — must be in place. The project’s configuration layering is as follows; initialization proceeds layer by layer with verification, not manual assembly.

LayerFile / MechanismLoading MethodPurpose
① Discipline SpecAGENTS.md “Multi-Agent Concurrent Git Commit Discipline”tracked, comes with checkout; natively loaded by CC / OpenCodeSurgical commits · Persistent slot no-push · No-delete worktree/branch · Commit format
② Hard Enforcement (Claude Code).claude/hooks/no-push-in-worktree.shPreToolUse(Bash) hookWhen cwd hits a slot, git … push → exit 2 block
② Hard Enforcement (OpenCode)opencode.jsonc → permission.bashConfig-layer hard denygit push*: deny / rm: deny
③ Capability Sharing.agents/skills/ (tool-neutral source, tracked)Per-Agent private <agent>/skills symlink entry (.gitignore-localized)One source, multiple entry points: when mixing Trae (.trae/skills), Claude Code CLI (.claude/skills), OpenCode (.opencode/skills), all point to the unified source .agents/skills/ via symlinks
④ Endpoint / Model.claude/settings.json + settings.*.json presets / opencode.jsoncenv + providerbaseURL convention per .agents/rules/endpoints.md (CC without /v1, OpenCode with /v1)
⑤ Full-Repo Searchgraphify MCPsettings mcp / opencode mcpSemantic location, replacing grep

How discipline is encoded into spec: Written rules alone aren’t enough — this project uses a soft constraint + hard enforcement dual-layer mechanism. AGENTS.md documents the discipline (Agents read and should comply), while the no-push-in-worktree.sh hook and opencode.jsonc permission provide physical interception (even if an Agent makes a mistake, it physically cannot push or delete). A single hook configuration is committed alongside settings.json, shared across all Worktrees, with differentiated enforcement based on cwd (the main repository master is not restricted).

Hard Enforcement Implementation: Source Code and Configuration (Claude Code)

Save the following universal interception script as .claude/hooks/no-push-in-worktree.sh (no project-specific modifications needed; it uses git rev-parse for dynamic, universal detection):

Workstation Initialization Instructions (Prompt Template)

Send this when launching claude / opencode CLI in a child slot or configuring in Trae (verify layer by layer; do not manually rebuild existing automation):

You are currently in a Git Worktree isolated CLI/IDE workstation slot (branch e.g. feature/claude). Please verify the workstation environment layer by layer:

  1. Discipline spec loaded: Confirm you have read AGENTS.md, recite the four “Multi-Agent Concurrent Git Commit Discipline” rules (surgical commits / persistent slot physically forbid push / forbid deleting worktree and branch / commit format <type>: description), and commit to complying for this session.
  2. Hard enforcement in place: Confirm .claude/hooks/no-push-in-worktree.sh exists and settings.json has registered this PreToolUse hook (on the OpenCode side, confirm opencode.jsonc contains git push: deny). Any git push from this workstation will be blocked; pushing is unified under the main repository master.
  3. Skill entry points in place: Confirm this workstation Agent’s private skills directory is symlinked to the neutral source .agents/skills/ — for mixed toolchains:
    • Trae: mkdir -p .trae && ln -sfn ../.agents/skills .trae/skills
    • Claude Code CLI: mkdir -p .claude && ln -sfn ../.agents/skills .claude/skills (or auto-created by SessionStart hook)
    • OpenCode CLI: Natively recognizes .agents/skills/ or symlink to .opencode/skills
  4. Endpoint configuration correct: Verify baseURL per .agents/rules/endpoints.md — Claude Code ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL without /v1, OpenCode provider baseURL with /v1; confirm current env points to the intended endpoint preset.
  5. Git status clean: git status confirms clean working tree, correct branch, and baseline at latest master.

4.2 Model and Custom Subscription/Endpoint Isolation SOP

For custom subscription configuration targeting Anthropic-compatible endpoints, the baseURL concatenation logic differs critically across CLI tools (must be strictly followed to avoid 404 errors):

  • OpenCode CLI (.opencode/opencode.jsonc):
    • Underlying SDK is @ai-sdk/anthropic, which automatically appends /messages to the baseURL.
    • baseURL must end with /v1 (e.g., https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/coding/v1 or https://.../api/anthropic/v1).
  • Claude Code CLI (.claude/settings.*.json):
    • Underlying SDK automatically appends /v1/messages to the baseURL.
    • ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL must NOT include /v1 (e.g., https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/coding).

5. Routine Automated Script Synchronization (Worktree-Sync)

After each CLI Agent completes its task and commits in its respective slot, the main workspace uses a script to perform one-click child branch merge and baseline refresh.

5.1 Automated Sync Script (scripts/worktree-sync.js)

Save the following code as scripts/worktree-sync.js in the main project:

6. When NOT to Use Script Sync (Boundaries and Pitfalls)

In the following 4 scenarios, script usage must be forbidden in favor of manual intervention:

❌ Scenario 1: Any Slot Has Uncommitted Changes (Dirty Tree)

  • Why: git rebase master requires a clean working tree. If an Agent is actively writing code without committing, the reverse rebase will either fail or mix dirty code into conflicts.
  • Action: First have the Agent complete its commit, or use git stash to temporarily shelve changes before syncing.

❌ Scenario 2: Code/Document Merge Conflicts (Merge / Rebase Conflict)

  • Why: When multiple Agents modify the same location in the same file, the worktree-sync.js script detects the conflict during git merge and safely aborts (reporting ❌ Branch [...] merge conflict detected).
  • Action and Lossless Superposition SOP:
    1. Stop immediately: After the script aborts, child slot Agents should make no changes — keep their commits as-is.
    2. Resolve in main workspace: The main Agent (or the user) opens the conflicting files in the master main workspace.
    3. Hard constraint: Lossless Superposition (A + B) Principle: Never take the lazy route of git checkout --ours/theirs or directly overwrite one side’s content! When merging, you must simultaneously preserve the valid code / Markdown sections from both Agent A and Agent B, using append or structured concatenation to fuse both modifications.
    4. Verify and recover: After resolving conflicts, run build/test commands (e.g., pnpm build) to verify no syntax breakage, then execute git commit, and re-run pnpm worktree:sync to complete the push and baseline sync.

❌ Scenario 3: Massive Refactoring or Destructive Directory Restructuring

  • Why: Cross-directory moves or batch file renames easily produce complex conflicts during automatic rebase.
  • Action: First complete the refactoring on master and commit, then manually enter each child Worktree and execute git rebase master.

❌ Scenario 4: Interactive Git States Requiring Manual Confirmation

  • Why: The script runs in non-interactive mode and cannot handle GPG signature prompts or SSH passphrase input.

7. Best Practices and Collaboration Discipline Summary (Four Golden Rules)

Multi-agent concurrent collaboration must strictly adhere to the following four non-negotiable red-line rules (encoded in AGENTS.md for mandatory enforcement):

  1. File Modification Isolation and Append Rule: Different Agents should modify different files whenever possible; if the same file must be modified, use append or precise targeted edits, and strictly forbid rewriting or clearing existing text.
  2. Surgical Commit Rule: Only git add <specific files for this task>, strictly forbid git add . / commit -a; verify the scope of changes before committing to prevent contaminating other Agents’ code.
  3. Persistent Slot Physical No-Push Rule: Child slots (project-claude / project-opencode, etc.) only perform local commits; physically forbid push and forbid deletion of Worktree/branch. git push is exclusively executed by the main workspace (master) after merge completion.
  4. Main Workspace Lossless Merge Rule (A + B): Merge conflicts are caught by the main repository’s worktree:sync; when resolving conflicts on master, the orchestrating Agent must follow the “Lossless Superposition (A + B)” principle, strictly forbidding overwriting or discarding either side’s valid changes, and must pass build verification after merging.

Appendix A: Quick Install Commands for Fully Compatible Agents

The following are quick install commands for the 5 🟢 fully compatible CLI Agents (source: official project documentation / repositories, verified 2026-08). After installation, launch each in its respective Worktree slot directory.

  • After installation, cd into each Worktree slot directory, configure baseURL per the endpoint convention (Claude Code without /v1, OpenCode with /v1; see Section 4.2), and launch the CLI Agent.

Appendix B: Real-World Walkthrough — End-to-End Validation with oh-my-pi

Using the 5th fully compatible tool, oh-my-pi (omp), as an example, this section walks through the full chain of «Install → Create Worktree Slot → Skill Assembly → Endpoint Configuration → Connectivity Verification» to validate the tutorial’s operability. All commands and configurations were verified through actual testing in 2026-08.

B.1 Prerequisite Awareness: The Compute Pool Is the Real Bottleneck for Concurrency

The hard bottleneck for multi-agent concurrency is not Worktree (the Git layer is nearly unlimited), but rather the TPM/RPM quotas of each AI coding subscription. Personal coding plan concurrency limits are generally low — running several slots simultaneously will quickly hit rate limits. Three approaches, in increasing ROI:

B.4 Architecture Evolution: Unified Compute Pool Gateway → Global Unified Endpoint

  • Current state (direct personal subscription): Each Agent uses its own key, endpoint configurations are scattered across project-level and global, TPM/RPM constrained by personal plan limits.
